An exemption lets the app keep working in deep sleep (e.g. for alarms, monitoring, sync). This usually costs noticeably more battery.

How strictly Android holds the app back in the background. Lower saves battery, but messages and sync may arrive later (approximate, depends on the Android version):
• Active: no limits.
• Now and then: background jobs wait up to ~8 h.
• Rare: jobs wait up to ~24 h, network is limited.
• Restricted: background work about once a day.
Sets every permission of this app to \"Block\" (camera, microphone, location, contacts, files …). Undo with \"All to default\".
The device could not change %1$d permissions
Notice when the configured protection is inactive
Shizuku is not running after the restart – the settings for %1$d apps have no effect until you start Shizuku.
Can\'t be disabled? Try other ways …

Some manufacturers block disabling their own apps. App Ops Shizuku tries, in this order, and stops at the first that works:
1. Disable until used (another disabled state).
2. Remove for this user – APK and data stay, restorable from the app list.
3. Hide as device owner – only if set up in Settings.
4. Neutralize – freeze, stop and block in the background. Weaker: the system can still start a frozen app in the background.
Every step is read back from the device.
Hidden as device owner. Restore it from the app list (\"hidden\").
The device allows neither disabling nor removing this app. It is now neutralized: frozen, stopped and blocked in the background. Undo: unfreeze it in this tab.
No way worked on this device. The device\'s answers:
Removed for this user. Restore it from the app list (\"removed\").
Disabled until used. Android may re-enable it if the app is started explicitly.
Type the package name to confirm:
The own app cannot be reset
Deletes the app\'s cache + data (login, settings, downloads) and resets permissions. Not reversible – for testing when an app hangs.
The own app cannot disable itself.
System app – disabling may impair other device functions.
The app will be stopped and removed from the launcher. Installed data is kept.
The app is stopped immediately and cannot be started – installed data is kept. To unfreeze, turn the switch off again.
Individual components only possible for apps with CHANGE_COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE (mostly system apps) – use \"Disable app\" for the icon
The own app cannot be disabled
System apps cannot be fully disabled
Harmless checks only: nothing is changed. The report contains model and Android version, no app list and no personal data.
Own text in the freeze dialog
Disabling was refused by the device: %1$s
The device did not take the setting.

Applies to every app (except apps with their own DNS-over-HTTPS). The provider sees which domains the device looks up – choose one you trust. Without a working provider there is no internet; \"Back to previous\" restores the old setting.
This is not a valid host name.

• %2$d apps with behavior settings (%3$d of them to be disabled or frozen)

Note: with a battery exemption Android sets the bucket itself to \"Exempted by system\". The bucket chosen above is then ignored and shown as \"not applied\" – that is expected, not an error.
Optimize app afterwards (takes a few seconds)
No saved original state – profile not applied yet.
Persistent notification while apps are paused on screen off
All %1$d values confirmed by the device.
Original state stays saved so you can try again.

For apps that must work reliably in the background (messenger, alarm clock, sync). Sets the cards above – standby bucket and battery exemption – plus permission to run in the background in one step, optionally also \"Optimize app\". The current state is saved first; \"Revert\" restores it.
Also available as a Quick Settings tile (edit tiles → \"Lockdown\"). System apps are never changed.
Lockdown off: %1$d given back, %2$d still open
Off. One tap takes the selected permissions away from all user apps; a second tap gives them back to exactly those apps.
The device did not take it back.
The app may only load data while you are using it. Recommended.
Puts the app on the background data restriction list (as with Data Saver).
Code scan: %1$d found, of which %2$d only in code.
Limit reached, not everything was searched.
Not all APK files were readable.
Display only. Searches for known components in the manifest and code. Obfuscated apps may rename library names – \"not found\" therefore remains a probability, not a guarantee.
The app\'s components could not be read.
That didn\'t work. The device did not apply the switch.
This stops network traffic, but not the tracker code in the app. Ads and analytics the app starts itself keep running. Only the APK patch (\"Camouflage\" tab) can really remove the code.
Not possible: Shizuku is not connected or not allowed.
The app will then be unable to load anything.
Not possible for system apps – Android only allows this for regular apps.
Nothing to reset. Nothing from this app has been changed here.

Found components cannot be disabled individually here – Android refuses this without root (the shell may not change the state of foreign components). Blocking is done via the three switches above; only the APK patch in the \"Camouflage\" tab removes code.
No network traffic recorded in the last 7 days.
Apps with much background traffic that you rarely open are listed first.
Needs usage access (granted via Shizuku). Connect Shizuku and reopen.
Only stop – opens from any launcher (Nova etc.). Weaker: other apps can start it on purpose.

Freezing only blocks opening. If the system or another app starts it in the background (e.g. a Bluetooth device connects), the watcher stops it again within about 5 minutes; only \"Disable\" prevents that completely.
Only apps you allowed may open locked apps. Start it via its shortcut instead.
\"%1$s\" wants to open apps you set to \"Only on demand\" (now: \"%2$s\"). App Ops Shizuku releases the app for this, just like via its shortcut, and locks it again after leaving.
Other apps may no longer open locked apps.
Only on demand (App Ops Shizuku): open this app via its home-screen shortcut – or choose the lock \"Only stop\" in App Ops Shizuku so any launcher works.
Blocked, but this device did not store "don\'t ask again" - the app may ask for the permission again.
Caution: deny may make the app crash on start (SecurityException). For the clipboard, ignore is the better choice (silent block).
%1$s: This app does not request the permission — nothing changed.
%1$s cannot be changed on this device – not applied.
Affects %1$d user apps: %2$s. System apps are left alone. Each app can be allowed again individually.
Blocked for %1$d apps, %2$d could not be changed
This setting can only be read with Shizuku connected.
Shizuku is not connected: view only, no access times.
App Ops Shizuku is not device owner (Settings → Device owner)
Not set. As device owner the app can hide system apps that the manufacturer will not let you disable or remove.
Active. \"Try other ways\" can now hide system apps. Hidden apps appear in the app list as \"(hidden)\".
All apps hidden by App Ops Shizuku are made visible again first, then the app gives up device owner. Afterwards it can be uninstalled normally.
Android refused: there are still accounts on the device. Remove them in Settings → Accounts, then try again.
Android refused: another app is already device owner. Only one is allowed.

Android only allows this when
• no accounts are on the device (Google, OnePlus, mail …) and
• there is only one user (no other users, no work profile).
Remove those in the system settings first – the app removes nothing itself. Afterwards you can add your accounts again.

As long as App Ops Shizuku is device owner it cannot be uninstalled; to remove it, first tap "Give up" here. It can also be set up from a PC: scripts/device-owner.sh in the repository.
App Ops Shizuku is now device owner. You can add your accounts again.
Android refused to make the app device owner.
Android refused: there are other users or a work profile. Remove them first (this deletes their data).
%1$s will be switched off for this app. Features that depend on it (e.g. autofill, smartwatch notifications) stop working. You can switch it on again in the system settings.
Current keyboard – change it in the system settings
These are not runtime permissions, but they let apps read the screen, notifications or everything you type.
The device did not take the change – use the system settings.

⚠ Start probe: error markers in log (%1$s). No crash detected, the app may be running with restrictions.
Start probe not possible: no launcher activity found. NOT checked whether the app starts.
Start probe not conclusive: no process of the app was seen in the log.
Start probe: app started, no crash markers in log within %1$d s (FATAL EXCEPTION, ClassNotFoundException, NoSuchMethodError, VerifyError, SecurityException).
Start probe not possible: the app could not be started (%1$s). NOT checked.
Start probe aborted: it did not respond after %1$d s (the app did not start cleanly). NOT checked — the patch itself is not affected.

Apps installed from now on get no background data, no clipboard access and may not run in the background until you release them (Permissions tab).\n\nChecked whenever you open this app, and immediately while the screen watcher is running. Requires Shizuku.
Quarantine for new apps is off. Apps already in quarantine stay there until released.
Not everything could be undone (Shizuku connected?). The app stays marked.
Quarantine: %1$d new app(s), %2$d not fully applied
This app is needed for the device to work (system, settings, phone, permissions, storage). It is not offered for removal.
This is your current home screen. Switch to another launcher first.
This is your current keyboard. Switch to another keyboard first.
Removed for this user – restore it from the app list

The app is removed from the main user only (pm uninstall -k --user 0). The APK stays in the system and its data is kept, so it can be restored at any time: it then appears in the app list as \"(removed)\" – tap it to restore. Removing system apps can affect other functions; restore the app if something stops working.
Pure entries go back to default. For permissions the permission is revoked — the app will ask again itself on next start. A permission is never granted automatically.
Set to default, %1$d entries not applied.
%1$s was removed for this user. Install it again from the system copy (cmd package install-existing)? Its data is still there.
Active when NOT connected to it
Reading the Wi-Fi name needs the location permission for this app (the app has no network access of its own).
Network name not readable (connected to Wi-Fi? location on?).
Rules run by time or Wi-Fi and need Shizuku to take effect. Wi-Fi rules may lag up to ~15 min (no always-on service).
Close (force stop) – the app is ended and gets no alarms or push messages until it is opened again; opening it stays possible
Freeze – the app cannot start at all until the screen is on again; data is kept
Not for apps the device needs to work (System UI, Settings, phone, launcher, keyboard, Shizuku …).
Not possible: Shizuku is not connected or not allowed.
Notifications are not allowed – the service still runs, but the notification is hidden.
Unfreeze when the screen turns on (otherwise it stays frozen until you unfreeze it at the top)
Service running. You can hide the notification (swipe it away or tap \"Hide\"); the service keeps working.

The opposite of the profile above: the app is stopped as soon as the screen turns off, so it cannot keep running in the background. Android only tells a running app about screen on/off, so while at least one app has this option, a service with a notification runs. You can hide the notification; the service keeps working. Default: off.
%1$s: not possible - Shizuku is not connected, no app was stopped

Newly installed apps get no background data, no clipboard and no background running until you release them.
Permission dialog not visible? Authorize this app in the Shizuku app under "Authorized apps".
Shizuku is not connected – nothing can be changed. Tap to open the settings.
The device did not take the change.
Not granted. Granted once via Shizuku, private DNS and revoking accessibility services keep working after a restart, without Shizuku running.
Granted: private DNS and revoking accessibility services work without Shizuku. Everything else still needs Shizuku.

Grant App Ops Shizuku permission in the Shizuku app.

In development (beta). Patching and disabling can damage the app. It is important to back up the app data before patching.\n\nThe patched app is signed with our own key — not with the manufacturer\'s or Google\'s key. As a result: no more Play updates, Play Protect may warn, and returning to the original app is only possible by reinstalling.
Installs the patched app as a parallel copy with its own package name — the original remains untouched and usable as normal. The clone has its own data and permissions.

Limits: Firebase (google_app_id) and AdMob (app ID) are bound to package name and signature — the clone may report registration errors or receive no ads. Apps with integrity checks (Play Integrity) may refuse to start. The clone starts with its own data (no login/history transfer).
An earlier clone %1$s is installed and will be updated (its data is kept).
The package name %1$s is already used by another app. Please choose a different name.
The app will be installed with a new signature. If the original is installed with a different signature, it will be uninstalled automatically — app data will be lost. Continue?

The app will be installed as a PARALLEL app (clone) with a new package name. The original remains untouched. The clone starts with its own data (no login/history transfer) and must be installed with a new signature. Continue?
Note: This app is an app bundle (split APKs, e.g. Google Maps). The clone copies all splits — this takes a bit longer and the clone will be correspondingly large.

Disable trackers (beta): components of the selected groups are disabled in the manifest (nothing is deleted). The app is then started once and checked for crashes for about 15 s; the number of disabled components is counted before and after.
Patches the app so that it never appears in the history (recent apps). Optionally the launcher icon is also removed. The app is re-signed in the process.
Android stopped the background service after its allowed running time. Please start the patch again.
No manifest change selected — please enable at least one option.
Progress and result of the stealth patch
Start probe: launching app, checking log…
Only runnable with an active VPN (VPN required)
Blank out content in history (incognito, like banking apps)
Important: The app will be re-signed. If the app is already installed, the original must be uninstalled first (app data will be lost).
Advertising ID: return a null ID (beta)
Spoofs device identity values ONLY in this app (smali call-site rewriting, no root required). Affects only the patched app, not the system.
Location: return a fixed city-level place (beta)
Stealth mode applied successfully — icon removed

Disables the components of the selected groups in the patched app\'s manifest (nothing is deleted) and sets the official Firebase switches. Push, WorkManager, payment and login remain untouched. The code of the building blocks stays in the app; building blocks without manifest components cannot be disabled this way.

Hides the app: removes it from history, removes the launcher icon, disguises it as a calculator (vault), device spoofing or cloning it as a parallel app. These features are for now still on the component screen.

Removes the selected permissions from the patched app\'s manifest. Unlike revoking, this is part of the installed app: it survives restarts, needs no running Shizuku, and the app cannot even ask for it again. The app has to cope with \"denied\" on its own — apps that need the internet stop working without it. Best used together with a clone.
Declared by this app: none of these permissions
Declared by this app: APK not readable

Remove permissions (beta): the selected permissions are removed from the manifest; the app gets \"denied\" for them permanently. The result is checked in the patched APK, then the app is started once and checked for crashes for about 15 s.
Without a clone, the patched app replaces the original; to get the permissions back you have to restore the original.
Remove permissions: the app declares none of the selected permissions — nothing was changed here.

Note app list: the app targets SDK %1$d. Android only filters the app list from targetSdk 30.

How strictly Android holds the app back in the background (approximate, depends on the Android version):
• Active: no limits.
• Regular: background jobs wait up to ~2 h.
• Now and then: jobs wait up to ~8 h, fewer alarms.

The app stays closed and locked. It only runs after you open it via its own shortcut on the home screen. When you leave it, it is closed and locked again after the chosen time – immediately when the screen turns off. Turning the screen on never releases it, so the app cannot wake itself up.
Freeze (pm suspend) – icon stays grey; can only be released with Shizuku
Disable (pm disable-user) – icon disappears; can also be re-enabled in the system settings without Shizuku
Only when the screen turns off
The app is now closed and locked. From then on it only runs when you open it via the shortcut (created next). While it is locked, messages, alarms and background sync of this app do not arrive.

Records crashes, failed Shizuku commands and internal errors – only on this device, nothing is sent (the app has no internet access). To report a problem, share the report or save it as a file. It contains device model, Android version and the package names of apps where something failed; read it before you send it.
App Ops Shizuku crashed last time. The details are in the error log. You can share the report there to report the problem.
Crashes and errors of this app, with share and save. Nothing is sent automatically.
Do not revoke while a foreground service is running
Applies to \"only while in use\": a running foreground service (e.g. music, navigation) keeps its permissions, because revoking would end the app. Revoked once the service stops. Default: off.
Auto-revoke of unused permissions: app is exempt (ignore) – not blocked
